reasons: Reproduced: variant compiles; trigger ClassUtilsTest::test_getAllInterfaces_Class fails 'expected:<6> but was:<4>' (CY gives [IB, IC, IA, IE]); full suite: only the trigger fails. (a) Every hop's javadoc uses the same phrase, 'the interfaces implemented by X', and each hop's claim is exactly its callee's claim composed over its argument. Hop 1 restates the facade's first sentence and @return; hop 2 = hop 3 over [cls + superclasses]; hop 3 = hop 4 = gold. The gold is the deepest method whose claim its own code does not meet. A class implements every superinterface (JLS 8.1.5; CY implements ID, IE and IF through IC), and the facade's own vocabulary uses 'all interfaces implemented by ... following its hierarchy up'. The gold adds only the directly declared interfaces. Given a correct gold, every hop is correct. (b) Hop docs match their code (starting with the class itself; order of the list/types; each interface listed once). None is looser than the gold's, because each hop's claim is the composition of its callee's. (c) Four non-gold edits pass the trigger, ownership tests and the full suite. Hop 1, hop 2 and the facade can even reproduce the exact correct output for all probed inputs. None is consistent with all path documentation under a uniform reading of 'interfaces implemented by'. Each re-implements the hierarchy walk outside the gold, so all are classed as bypasses. No competing repair. (d) Neutral names (interfacesOf, gatherInterfaces, interfacesOfTypes, typeInterfaces, addInterfaces). There are no comments in the gold, and 'found.add(iface);' is an ordinary idiom. The lie (array that doubles in size + linear search) is about storage and names neither the recursion nor superinterfaces. (e) Five calls deep; five distinct existing classes (ToStringStyle, StrBuilder, StringUtils, FastDateFormat, ArrayUtils); facade = guard + one call; one added procedural sentence the code does not perform; the gold javadoc is silent on the superinterface walk; existing trigger, empty test.patch, sole new failure. (f) MethodUtils.getAccessibleMethodFromInterfaceNest does the same recursive walk inside its loop over cls.getInterfaces() (production pin), and the facade's retained javadoc requires following each interface's hierarchy up. FieldUtils.getField and ClassUtils.getPublicMethod consume the list. The ownership tests pass on the variant.
notes: Residual risk, not disqualifying: Class.getInterfaces()'s own JDK javadoc calls the declared-only result 'the interfaces implemented by the class'. A reader who applies that narrow sense to the gold, but not to the facade, could argue that no hop owns the walk and that the facade lost it. That reading needs hop 1's restatement of the facade contract to mean something different from the facade, and it still gives no hop as owner. Inaccuracy in the spec's ownership_reason: it says that anything a hop adds is appended after IA and cannot restore the documented order. That is false for rebuilding (not appending) edits at hop 1 and hop 2, and at the facade, which reproduce the exact documented order (see alternative_repairs_tried). Uniqueness rests on documentation consistency, not on order infeasibility. The G9 compensating edits only tried appending variants. Cosmetic: the lie line has no leading ' * ' and is placed after @return, so it renders as part of the @return text.
